title: unify-session-grace-and-stream-drain-crosssdk
author: Ava Chen
release_notes: Aligned session grace/reauth defaults across Python/TS/Go SDKs, added ergonomic stream drain helpers, fixed an edge case that could cause stalled drains when token refresh overlaps generation. Minor version bumps for all SDKs.
description: Context: Teams reported subtle production flakes where long-running streaming sessions would deadlock while the SDK attempted token refresh near connection shutdown. Root cause: mismatched defaults across languages (py: grace=5s, ts: grace=2s, go: none) combined with non-deterministic drain logic in the stream consumer. Motivation: provide predictable, cross-language semantics for credential grace windows and give app authors explicit, ergonomic controls for draining streaming responses. What this PR does: 1) introduce a unified config property 'session_grace_ms' (default 5000) surface on all SDK clients; SDKs continue to accept language-idiomatic names but map to the canonical value in shared test fixtures. 2) add 'stream_drain_timeout_ms' with a default of 3000 to guard shutdown path; streaming helpers now expose drain_until_eof(timeout_ms) convenience methods on Python/TS and DrainWithContext(ctx, timeoutMs) on Go. 3) refactor token refresh handshake to be cancelable and cooperative with drain: refresh now registers a short-lived lease and yields shutdown precedence to drain paths. 4) add cross-sdk integration tests that simulate concurrent refresh and EOF arrival, and a stress test harness that reproduces the original deadlock pattern. 5) bump package versions: python 1.9.0, typescript 2.6.1, go 1.4.0 (minor/patch bumps only). Checklist: - [x] design doc (ENG-1842) and UX doc reviewed - [x] unit tests added for all three SDKs - [x] crosslang integration test added to perf lab - [x] reviewed and approved by SDK leads - [x] release notes drafted Testing and CI: initial CI run showed a flaky TS streaming test (stream-drain-signal) — reproduced locally, fixed race by moving the drain signal to the top-level loop and adding a short backoff in the TS connector. All CI checks green on rerun. Migration notes: default values are conservative; existing callers should be unaffected. If teams relied on the previous lower grace intervals, they can set session_grace_ms explicitly. Operational notes: this change reduces rare stalled streams at the cost of a modestly longer shutdown window in some workloads; metrics added to the Console: sdk.session.grace_ms_applied and sdk.stream.drain_timeout_ms_applied. Rollout plan: quick canary to ~10% of hosted SDK traffic for 48h, then gradual increase. If we see an uptick in shutdown latency beyond expectations, we will roll back and revert to per-sdk defaults while we iterate. Related: SUP-4021 (customer incident), ENG-1842 design doc.

review_comments: Omar Reyes: Can you explain why 5s was chosen as the default? Is it empirically driven?
Ava Chen: Chose 5s after running the stress harness under realistic network jitter; it covered 99.7% of reproductions while keeping shutdown latency acceptable. Added note in UX doc.
Nina Patel: TS test was flaky in CI — I see you added the backoff, please add a short comment explaining the tradeoff so it's not removed by future authors.
Ava Chen: Added inline comment and extracted backoff as 'drainYieldBackoffMs' constant with a unit test asserting > 95% success over 500 runs.
Soren Li: Approve after the changelog bump. Observability: can we emit a metric when refresh yields to drain?
Ava Chen: Added metric sdk.refresh.yield_to_drain with counts and labels (sdk_lang, client_id).

notes_for_backport: Backport to release/1.9.x (python) and release/2.6.x (typescript) recommended if teams want immediate fix in older branches; go change is non-breaking and can be cherry-picked.
manual_steps: After deploy: watch sdk.session.grace_ms_applied and sdk.stream.drain_timeout_ms_applied in Console for anomalies; if shutdown latency rises, temporarily set session_grace_ms to previous per-sdk value and open support ticket.
